title: PM Auguste Adib resigns after senators petition against his cabinet
why: The first Lebanese prime minister goes on 2 May; Bechara Khoury forms the next cabinet on 5 May 1927.

title: Bechara Khoury forms his second cabinet
why: Third government of Greater Lebanon; the Lebanese University table also dates it 5/1/1928.

title: Khayreddin Ahdab forms his second cabinet
why: Formed two months after his first; the Lebanese University table gives 14 March (other sources: 14 March).

title: Khayreddin Ahdab forms his third cabinet
why: Third Ahdab government under President Eddé, per the Lebanese University table of governments. (corrected from 1937-07-10, which is the start of his first cabinet; UL table: third Ahdab government from 13/1/1938 to 21/3/1938)

title: Ahdab forms national unity cabinet with both blocs
why: Four National Bloc and three Constitutional Bloc ministers; it won parliament confidence with 56 votes.

title: Three ministers resign from the Ahdab unity cabinet
why: Salim Takla, Majid Arslan and Habib Abou Chahla quit; Eddé replaced them with National Bloc men, angering Constitutionalists.

title: Ahdab forms fifth cabinet as a reshuffle
why: Counted as a new cabinet at Constitutional Bloc request; it won confidence on 18 January, 38 votes to 13.

title: Khayreddin Ahdab resigns as prime minister
why: Ends his fifth cabinet; Khaled Chehab takes over the same day.

title: Khaled Chehab forms his first cabinet
why: Thirteenth government of the mandate; ministerial statement 25 March, confidence 41 to 14 (other sources: 18 March).

title: Khaled Chehab first cabinet ends
why: The page gives 27 October 1938 as its last day; the Lebanese University table has the next cabinet from 1 November.

title: Abdallah Yafi forms his second cabinet
why: A new Yafi cabinet within the 1938-39 run, per the Lebanese University table.

title: Ayoub Tabet government ends
why: Tabet leaves office on 21 July 1943; Petro Trad heads the caretaker government from 1 August.

title: Riad Solh forms his second cabinet
why: First cabinet of independent Lebanon lasted from 25 September 1943 to 3 July 1944.

title: Riad Solh forms a new cabinet
why: Part of Solh's 1946-51 premiership, recorded as a separate government in the Lebanese University table.

title: Riad Solh forms another cabinet
why: Part of Solh's 1946-51 premiership, recorded as a separate government in the Lebanese University table.

title: Riad Solh forms his last cabinet of the decade
why: Part of Solh's 1946-51 premiership, recorded as a separate government in the Lebanese University table.

title: Fouad Chehab forms emergency military cabinet
why: Formed by Decree 9444 and ran until 30 September, overseeing the election of Khoury's successor.

title: Khaled Chehab forms second cabinet under Chamoun
why: Formed 30 September 1952 and dissolved 30 April 1953 (other sources: 1 October).

title: Abdallah Yafi forms a new cabinet
why: Separate government in the Lebanese University table of cabinets, within the same prime minister's run.

title: Sami Solh forms a new cabinet
why: Separate government in the Lebanese University table of cabinets, within the same prime minister's run.

title: Abdallah Yafi forms another cabinet
why: Separate government in the Lebanese University table of cabinets, within the same prime minister's run.

title: Sami Solh forms a new cabinet
why: Separate government in the Lebanese University table of cabinets, within the same prime minister's run.

title: Sami Solh forms a new cabinet in the crisis year
why: Separate government in the Lebanese University table of cabinets, within the same prime minister's run.

title: Saeb Salam forms a new cabinet
why: The table ends his first 1960 cabinet on 20/5/1961; the next row mistypes the start as 1960.

title: Hussein Oweini forms a new cabinet under Helou
why: First cabinet after Charles Helou took office on 23 September 1964.

title: Hussein Oweini forms another cabinet
why: Third Oweini cabinet row in the Lebanese University table.

title: Abdallah Yafi forms a new cabinet
why: The first of two Yafi cabinets of autumn 1968 (12-20 October); the second formed on 20 October.

title: Abdallah Yafi forms another cabinet
why: Second change of cabinet in eight days under Yafi.

title: Rashid Karami forms a new cabinet
why: Karami's second cabinet of 1969, after the clashes over Palestinian guerrillas.

title: Saeb Salam forms a new cabinet after the 1972 elections
why: Ran to 25 April 1973 (corrected from "last government formed before the civil war began", which the table does not support).

title: Salim Hoss forms second cabinet
why: The first Hoss cabinet page shows dissolution on 2 July 1979; the Lebanese University table dates the second from 16 July.

title: Shafik Wazzan forms second cabinet under Amine Gemayel
why: Reformed after Bashir Gemayel's assassination and the 21 September election of Amine Gemayel.

title: Salim Hoss cabinet takes office under President Hrawi
why: Day after Hrawi's election; Aoun's rival military cabinet kept ruling Baabda, hence two governments.

title: Aoun's military cabinet ends as Syrian forces take Baabda
why: Wikipedia gives 13 October 1990 as the end of Michel Aoun's disputed premiership.

title: Rafic Hariri forms his second cabinet
why: His first cabinet was dissolved on 25 May 1995; the Lebanese University table starts the next that day.

title: Rafic Hariri forms his third cabinet
why: Formed after the 1996 elections, per the Lebanese University table of governments.

title: Rafic Hariri forms his fifth cabinet
why: Sixty-sixth government since independence; it resigned on 26 October 2004 over Lahoud's extension.

title: Siniora government becomes interim as Lahoud's term ends
why: No new president had been elected, so the cabinet continued as a caretaker one.

title: Hariri's second cabinet is considered resigned after elections
why: Constitution treats the cabinet as resigned after parliament elections; the third Hariri cabinet formed only on 31 January 2019.

title: First extension of the 1972 parliament
why: Under Frangieh; the 14th term was extended twice, by Laws 1/76 and 3/78, to 30 June 1980.
dup_of: Parliament's mandate extended during civil war

title: Parliament extends its own term a second time
why: Under Sarkis; Law 3/78 extends the 1972 chamber to 30 June 1980.

title: Parliament extends its term for the third time
why: Law 14/80 starts the 15th four-year term, extended again in 1983.

title: Parliament extends its term under Amine Gemayel
why: Law 9/83; the 15th term ran to December 1984.

title: Parliament extends its term again
why: Law 3/84 opens the 16th four-year term of the 1972 chamber.

title: Parliament extends its term for the sixth time
why: Law 11/86; the 16th term ran to December 1988. (corrected from "fifth": Al Jazeera counts 1976, 1978, 1980, 1983, 1984, 1986, 1987, 1989)

title: Parliament extends its term for the seventh time
why: Law 25/87 opens the 17th term, extended again by Law 1/89. (corrected from "sixth": Al Jazeera counts 1976, 1978, 1980, 1983, 1984, 1986, 1987, 1989)

title: Last wartime extension, to December 1994 on paper
why: Law 1/89 under Hrawi; the 1992 election law ended it early.

title: The 1972 parliament begins its record 19-year life
why: The 13th chamber, sworn in 3 May 1972, sat until May 1991, the longest in Lebanese history.

title: Law 51 amends election law and adds new parliamentary seats
why: Follows the 1990 constitutional amendment (Law 18 of 21 Sept 1990) implementing Taif.

title: Decree 1307 appoints 55 deputies to fill vacant and new seats
why: Parliament grows to 108 seats split equally between Christians and Muslims; later raised to 128.

title: Parliament passes the post-war election law
why: The 1972 chamber is treated as dissolved from October 1992, after 20 years in office.

title: Aoun decrees the dissolution of parliament
why: Issued the day before Parliament met at Qoleiat; deputies and Syria rejected it.

title: Arrete 2/LR sets size and method of the Chamber of Deputies
why: Fixes composition and election method of the Chamber; amended 4 May and 3 December 1934.

title: Chamber of Deputies elections held under the restored constitution
why: Libnanews dates the general elections to 20 January 1934 (another account: first polling day 22 January).

title: Charles Debbas elected speaker of the Chamber
why: Held until 31 October 1934, after leaving the presidency on 2 January; Petro Trad succeeded him.

title: Arrete 95/LR amends the 1934 election rules
why: First amendment to Arrete 2/LR on the Chamber of Deputies.

title: Arrete 279/LR amends the election rules again
why: Second 1934 amendment; arretes of 1937 followed, and the 1943 text kept these rules.

title: Sarkis elected at the Esseily villa as parliament cannot sit
why: Elected on the second round with 66 votes; 29 deputies boycotted; the chamber building was unsafe.

title: Sarkis takes office; oath in a Shtaura hotel
why: Wikipedia says the oath could not be held in parliament and was taken at a hotel in Shtaura (oath date not stated).

title: Bashir Gemayel elected at the Fayyadiyeh Military Academy
why: Venue chosen for the session; 62 of 92 deputies attended, he won the second round with 57 votes.

title: Amine Gemayel elected with 77 votes among 80 deputies present
why: Venue not confirmed in the pages read; 3 blank ballots.

title: Parliament meets at Qoleiat air base and elects Moawad
why: 52 of 58 attending deputies; the venue was far from Aoun-held Baabda, and Aoun denied its validity.

title: Parliament meets at the Park Hotel in Chtaura, elects Hrawi
why: Elected by 47 of 52 attending deputies two days after Moawad's assassination; he promised to sign Taif into law.

title: UNSC Resolution 129 calls emergency session on Lebanon complaint
why: Adopted unanimously after Council deadlock; sends the matter to a General Assembly emergency special session.

title: UNSC Resolution 262 condemns Israel after hearing Lebanon
why: Unanimous; condemns premeditated military action and warns Israel against further attacks.

title: UNSC Resolution 270 condemns Israeli air attack on south Lebanon
why: Condemns Israel and deplores ceasefire violations.

title: UNSC Resolution 279 demands Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon
why: At 15 words, the second-shortest resolution ever adopted.

title: UNSC Resolution 280 condemns Israel's military action in Lebanon
why: Reaffirms earlier resolutions and condemns premeditated action.

title: UNSC Resolution 285 demands full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon
why: At 14 words, the shortest resolution ever adopted.

title: UNSC Resolution 313 demands Israel stop action against Lebanon
why: Demands an end to ground and military action and withdrawal of forces.

title: UNSC Resolution 316 condemns Israeli attacks on Lebanon
why: Calls on Israel to abide by earlier resolutions.

title: UNSC Resolution 317 on abducted Syrian and Lebanese personnel
why: Deplores Israel's failure to release personnel seized by its forces.

title: UNSC Resolution 332 condemns the 1973 Israeli raid on Lebanon
why: Adopted after a Lebanese complaint; grieves loss of civilian life.

title: UNSC Resolution 337 condemns Israel for seizing a Lebanese airliner
why: Unanimous; the Council called the diversion and seizure a violation of Lebanese sovereignty.

title: UNSC Resolution 347 condemns Israeli violation of Lebanese territory
why: Adopted over fears the violence would widen to war.

title: UNSC Resolution 490 calls for end of Israeli attacks on Lebanon
why: Unanimous; demands respect for territorial integrity and a report within 48 hours.

title: UNSC Resolution 513 on humanitarian crisis in West Beirut
why: Unanimous; demands respect for civilians and restoration of water, power and food.

title: UNSC Resolution 515 demands Israel lift the Beirut blockade
why: 14 votes to none; the United States did not vote and Israel did not comply.

title: UNSC Resolution 519 adds humanitarian tasks to UNIFIL mandate
why: Extends UNIFIL to 19 October 1982 and authorises humanitarian work; Poland and USSR abstained.

title: UNSC Resolution 542 demands ceasefire in north Lebanon
why: Unanimous; concerned by fighting in the north and loss of life.

title: UNSC Resolution 564 on violence against civilians and camps
why: Unanimous; urges ICRC and UNRWA aid after fighting involving Palestinian camps.

title: UNSC Resolution 587 condemns attacks on UNIFIL
why: Demands withdrawal of forces not accepted by Lebanese authorities from the south.

title: UNSC Resolution 618 condemns abduction of Lt Col William Higgins
why: Unanimous; demands the release of the UN observer seized in south Lebanon.

title: UNSC Resolution 1052 calls for ceasefire in Operation Grapes of Wrath
why: Unanimous; adopted the day of the Qana shelling of a UNIFIL base.

title: UNSC Resolution 2650 renews UNIFIL and restates freedom-of-movement rule
why: Reaffirms that under the SOFA UNIFIL needs no prior authorization or permission for mandated tasks; extended to 31 August 2023.
